subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Engineering Ethics in the Age of AI
description: A fast breakdown of Engineering Ethics in the Age of AI for builders.

hook.text: When a self-driving car must choose between two bad outcomes, who wrote the code that decides? And who takes the blame?

buildup.text: Traditional ethics assumed a human made decisions. AI systems make thousands of choices per second with no human in the loop.

discovery.text: Algorithmic bias reflects the data it's trained on. If historical data is biased, the AI will be biased — at scale and at speed.

twist.text: Autonomous weapons select and engage targets without human approval. The engineering community is divided on building them.

climax.text: IEEE and ACM published ethical guidelines for AI engineers. But guidelines without enforcement are just suggestions.

punchline.text: The code decides. The engineer who wrote it bears responsibility — even unwatched.

quiz.question: Why is algorithmic bias a concern in AI-driven engineering systems?
options: AI systems deliberately choose biased outcomes to maximize efficiency
If trained on biased historical data, the AI reproduces that bias at scale and speed
Programmers intentionally code preferences into AI systems for commercial advantage
